questions.prompt: A guest slips on a wet floor but says they're fine. What must happen, and by when?
questions.modelAnswer: Any injury, however minor, is an incident. Make the area safe, notify the Duty Manager immediately, collect facts (who, what, where, when, witnesses, photos), and file the Incident Report the same shift. Don't offer compensation or admit liability.
keyPoints: File the Incident Report the same shift
Facts only, no compensation or admission of liability

questions.prompt: Does a near miss with no injury need a report? Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: Yes. Near misses — something that could have caused injury, like a wet floor or loose railing — count as incidents. Notify the Duty Manager by end of shift and file the report the same shift.
keyPoints: Yes, near misses count as incidents

questions.prompt: The fire alarm sounds. List what you do, including what you take with you.
questions.modelAnswer: Treat it as real. Call the Duty Manager to confirm the fire department has been called; if you can't reach anyone within 1 minute, call 911 yourself. Take the arrivals/in-house list to the assembly point, direct guests to the nearest exit and never to elevators, account for guests using the list, and don't re-enter until cleared.
keyPoints: Call 911 yourself if no answer within 1 minute
Account for guests at the assembly point

questions.prompt: A guest collapses and isn't breathing. What are your first three actions?
questions.modelAnswer: Call 911 first, then call the Duty Manager, then send someone to meet the ambulance at the entrance. Get the AED and follow its prompts; stay with the person.
keyPoints: Send someone to meet the ambulance

questions.prompt: What are the first two things to check in a power outage?
questions.modelAnswer: That the emergency lighting came on, then the elevators for trapped guests — call the elevator emergency line if anyone is inside.
